corrections.text: The article states the most common adverse events were "decreased appetite, nausea, rash, headache, and abdominal pain in children and adolescents." Otsuka's press release actually differentiates by age band: children aged 6 to 12 experienced only rash and decreased appetite, while the fuller list of decreased appetite, nausea, rash, headache, and abdominal pain applies specifically to adolescents aged 13 to 17. The article's merged wording overstates the adverse events reported for the younger age group.
